Okay, now that the Hello World sequence is complete, I feel more comfortable reading this one.

Which leads to the question, when exactly does this fit into the timeline established by Hello World? Because unless I'm misunderstanding something, this MTF wasn't formed until the express purpose of reacting to the Maxwellist thing, which and then they events of Hello World happened pretty much immediately before culminating in such a way as to preclude the presence of one of the characters presented here1.

I like this story, but I'm confused by the timeline.

item.content:encoded:
Echoing others on cliché-ness of plot elements and characters. 8-ball continues to be my standout favorite. Some parts are fine, but some things that could be more interesting (like, what an AI's perspective would be when hacking/fighting other AIs) are forsaken for things that, paradoxically, seem more limiting (simulspace in other tales, the game thing in this one).

Visually pleasing, but predictability makes it a slog to read.

item.content:encoded:
The biggest problem I've had with the adventures of Kappa-10 is that everyone follows such well-trodden character beats that it's impossible to be surprised by the characters at all.

This is no different. Grape's backstory is absolutely laden with cliches, from playing games with a rogue AI to hiding a heart of gold under his vitriolic attitude to being blood brothers with the group's Snake Eyes. I actually rolled my eyes at several points.

But it's also damn well presented and fun to read.
